references.text: Abram camps between Bethel and Ai and builds an altar there to the Lord—the place that Jacob later formally names Bethel.
God commands Jacob to go to Bethel. Jacob travels there, builds an altar, and the place is called El-Bethel—a confirmation of the naming in 28:19.
Jacob tells Joseph that God Almighty appeared to him at Luz in the land of Canaan—a direct reference back to the event in 28:19.
Joshua describes Judah's border as going down to Luz, 'that is Bethel'—confirming the name change from Luz to Bethel.
The house of Joseph spies on Luz, and the text explains that the city's former name was Luz—a confirmation of the naming in Genesis 28:19.
Hosea mentions Bethel as the place where God found Jacob and spoke with him—a prophetic reference back to Jacob's experience in Genesis 28.
This verse shows an ironic parallel where the city reappears under its old pagan name Luz, in contrast to Jacob's consecration of the place as Bethel.
Confirms and expands on the same event where Jacob names the place Bethel after God's revelation.
Confirms the identity of the place Luz/Bethel in connection with Jacob's arrival.
